newsitem.title: USA: U.S. energy prices extend daytime rally on storms.
newsitem.headline: U.S. energy prices extend daytime rally on storms.

text.p: U.S. energy futures prices continued their rally in after hours trade on continuing fears that hurricanes and tropical storms could disrupt supplies in the Carribean, especially Amerada Hess' huge refinery.
October NYMEX traded at $22.25 a barrel on ACCESS, up 10 cents from the close with September seeing 600 lots trade early.
"It's going up with all the news on the weather," one trader said. "With three hurricanes in the cycle you never know."
September gasoline, which expires on Friday, gained 0.28 cent to reach 64 cents a gallon on ACCESS.
This added to the 1.63-cent rise seen during the day, with 100 lots out of a total of 250 trading in the front month.
September heating oil rose 0.08 cent a gallon to 63.75 cents on 100 lots traded.
Most activity occurred in later futures contracts, with October heating oil seeing 300 lots change hands out of the total 530 traded early in ACCESS.
